Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise confirmation we typically provide for pilots; happy to expand any section or provide a short diagram for your risk doc. I copied Rishi from Product/Sales to help with any contractual options (retention limits, DPA changes, CMK).

Redwood confirmation (pilot scope):
- What we store: by default Redwood stores prompt text, output text, basic request metadata (timestamp, model, model_version, request_id). We do not store full requestor IPs in the same logs by default; we record region and anonymized usage metrics.
- Storage location: data for pilot accounts in the hosted environment is stored in our US region (AWS us-west-2) unless a customer requests EU residency. For Dedicated/Private deployments, data remains in the customer's VPC/region.
- Retention: default retention for prompts and outputs is 90 days for hosted trial accounts (used for debugging, billing reconciliation, and regression monitoring). Request metadata (non-PII aggregation) is kept for 365 days. We can offer shorter retention windows (30 days or 0 days for outputs/prompts) under a contractual amendment for pilots.
- Logging & access controls: access to raw prompt/output data is limited to a small set of SRE/product engineers for incident response; all access is audited. We emit structured audit logs and can produce redaction/obfuscation on ingest for specific fields.
- Redaction & no-logging options: customers can enable automatic redaction on ingest (pattern-based or field-mapping) and can opt into a "no-persist" mode where prompts/outputs are not written to long-term storage (best-effort, short-lived in-memory KV cache only). For compliance-sensitive pilots, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment + CMK.
- Encryption & keys: data at rest is encrypted with AWS KMS-managed keys by default; we support customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM) with Private deployments or enterprise contracts.
- Certifications / Docs: we are SOC 2 Type II and provide a DPA and standard security questionnaire. See attached security whitepaper for details and the link below.

If this matches what you need, say so and we'll prepare a one-page sign-off for your security team to include in the pilot packet. If you want stricter retention or residency, Rishi and I can scope update options and cost impact.

Thanks — quick clarifications below (happy to jump on a 20-min call if you prefer):

1) Request metadata vs PII:
   - Request metadata: request_id, model, model_version, timestamp, region, request_latency, anonymized usage metrics. These are considered operational telemetry and are stored separately from prompt/output blobs.
   - PII in prompts/outputs: any customer-provided identifiers (user_id, email, SSN, medical record numbers) that appear in prompt or generated output are treated as PII. We do not automatically parse or remove those unless you enable redaction. By default, the raw prompt and generated output (which may include PII) are retained per the retention policy above.

2) No-persist mode:
   - No-persist mode prevents writing prompts and outputs to our long-term object store. Requests are processed in-memory and short-lived caches (KV cache) may exist for performance during the session and are evicted immediately after use. No-persist also excludes prompts/outputs from automated logging and analytics pipelines. Note: some ephemeral traces (request_id and operational telemetry) are retained for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation but do not contain prompt/output text.

3) CMK availability:
   - Customer-managed keys (CMK) are available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted shared accounts we can offer application-layer encryption for certain fields but full KMS CMK (customer key in customer's account) requires Dedicated or Private (we can scope a hybrid option for short pilots).
